stage_a.note: Enthusiastic engagement characterizes most of the presentation alongside some mixed interactions.
Pronounced, sustained engagement and excitement characterize the presentation across its substantive content.
An approachable, friendly orientation is apparent at several points alongside more impersonal, serious delivery.

venture.description: Premium wine served in a patented single-serve sealed glass.
venture.note: The founder is seeking investment to build a second bottling line to keep up with demand.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James delivers his prepared presentation, detailing his explosive sales growth and the need for capital to build a second line.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks James if he has reconsidered his refusal to license the single-serve wine technology to the broader industry.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James deflects the licensing question by presenting a custom-labeled wine bottle he created specifically to mock Kevin.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks James to confirm the exact terms of the offer he walked away from during his previous appearance.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James confirms that Kevin had previously offered him six hundred thousand dollars for a fifty-one percent stake in the patents.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin states that he still believes his previous offer was a great deal for the business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asserts that James made a mistake by walking away from the previous offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James jokes about the investors having good memories of his previous pitch.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond jokes with James, warning him that the panel will not be as gentle as they were last time.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James jokes back that he does not remember the panel being gentle during his first appearance.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond insists that their previous treatment of James was indeed gentle.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James defends his previous decision, stating he has now proven the brand's value and increased the worth of his patents.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin jokes about his previous comment calling James a dead man walking, asking if he is now a ghost.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James shows the panel a custom wine bottle featuring a label that reads dead man walking.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin proposes a strategy to license the technology to the top three wine players, claiming it would quadruple James's wealth.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks Kevin to clarify if he is proposing the exact same offer he made during James's first appearance.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin confirms he is making the same offer of six hundred thousand dollars for fifty-one percent.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond recalls James passing out wine during his first pitch and asks him to do so again.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James hands out samples of his single-serve wine to the panel to demonstrate the ease of the product.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond states he was not interested in the business last time and is exiting the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin expresses a desire to stop fighting and find a way to partner with James on the valuable technology.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark states he is uncomfortable with the six million dollar valuation and asks James to be flexible on the equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James agrees to negotiate and attempts to justify his valuation by comparing his business to other national brands.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara states she still has a negative visceral reaction to James and exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark reiterates that the panel values the company lower than James does and asks him to adjust his valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James acknowledges their interest and expresses a willingness to work on the valuation to reach a deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin offers three hundred thousand dollars for twelve percent equity, valuing the company at exactly two and a half million.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert clarifies with Kevin that his offer implies a two and a half million dollar valuation for the company.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin confirms that he believes the company is worth exactly two and a half million dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin urges James to accept the offer, emphasizing the tremendous global potential of the business with his involvement.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark advises James to make a phone call before deciding, suggesting he might be able to improve the offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark proposes to Kevin and Robert that they team up to offer more money for a thirty percent stake.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara comments to the other investors, anticipating James's reaction when he returns to the room.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks James who he spoke with on the phone during his break from the pitch.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James answers that he called Jim Koch, the founder of a major beer company.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks James what advice Jim Koch gave him regarding the negotiation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James explains that Jim advised him to ensure any new partner shares his vision for the company.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks if Jim Koch is an investor or equity owner in the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James clarifies that Jim is an advisor and does not hold any equity in the company.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark challenges James, asking why Jim did not simply provide the capital if the business is so promising.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James defends Jim's role, stating that the best advice comes from an unbiased party without a financial stake.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks James what Jim advised him to do regarding Kevin's offer of three hundred thousand for twelve percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James counters Kevin's offer, proposing three hundred thousand dollars for an eight percent stake based on Jim's advice.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks James to confirm if that is his final counter-offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James confirms that eight percent is his counter-offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark informs James that he is not interested in the counter-offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James asks Mark to explain why he is not interested in the eight percent equity stake.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark explains that eight percent does not provide enough equity for the investors to be fully committed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James argues that he has his own valuation for the company, just as the investors have theirs.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark presents a joint offer with Robert and Kevin for six hundred thousand dollars in exchange for thirty percent equity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert points out that the joint offer provides twice the capital James originally requested.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James asks if partnering with Mark would guarantee his product placement in Mark's sports stadium.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark states he cannot guarantee stadium placement just because they have a service organization.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark warns James that he is overthinking the deal and needs to make a decision immediately.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond advises James not to make the same mistake he made during his first pitch.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert emphasizes the unique opportunity James has with three investors willing to partner with him.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James expresses concern about Kevin constantly pressuring him to split or sell the company.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert reassures James that he and Mark will manage Kevin and urges James to make a decision.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James states he wants to partner but is hesitant to give up thirty percent without guaranteed stadium placement.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark reiterates that James simply needs to make a decision on the offer presented.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert states they have made a fair offer and pressures James to give them an answer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James opens a bottle of wine, calling it a million-dollar bottle.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin reminds James that the offer requires giving up thirty percent of the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James argues that giving up thirty percent means selling a large portion of his company at a significant discount.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin tells James he is not thinking clearly about the value the investors bring to the business.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert interprets James's actions as a sign that he is going to accept the offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks James to clearly state his decision.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin suggests they drink the wine together to celebrate the deal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert again asks James to explicitly state what he is deciding.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James rejects the joint offer and decides to walk away from the deal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark expresses frustration with James's behavior, accusing him of playing games, and exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: James defends his actions, stating he came seeking a partnership at a reasonable valuation determined by experts.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond challenges James by pointing out that none of those experts actually invested money in his company.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark reiterates that a company is only worth what someone is willing to pay and confirms his exit.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond asks Robert and Kevin if they plan to split the deal without Mark.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert states that James wasted their time and exits the negotiation.

decisions.note: Reiterates his previous offer of $600k for 51% to license the technology to major players.
Was not interested last time and is just watching the interaction for entertainment.
Has a negative visceral reaction to the founder and does not like him.
Believes the company is worth exactly $2.5 million and offers accordingly.
Advised by Jim Koch that the company is worth more than the offer presented.
Mark, Robert, and Kevin team up to offer $600k for 10% equity each.
Wants a guarantee of stadium entry and feels 30% is too much equity to give up.
Thinks the founder is playing games and creating unnecessary drama.
Feels the founder just came to waste their time without serious intent to deal.

record.notes: A phone call insert with Jim Koch is shown during the pitch; it is recorded as an excluded span since he is not present in the room.
